description: An interactive categorization tool for Grade 7 Science where students classify 9 real-world actions into 'Depletes Groundwater' (harmful) or 'Recharges Groundwater' (helpful). Students apply cause-and-effect reasoning about infiltration to determine each action's impact on groundwater levels. Features drag-and-drop + tap-to-sort interaction, immediate feedback with explanations/hints, score tracking, animated cross-section illustrations per step (including an animated bore-well pump in Step 2), and a split-screen completion summary with underground cross-sections showing water table levels.
subject: Science
teaching_notes: Activate AFTER discussing both groundwater depletion causes and rainwater harvesting solutions. Watch for tricky items: deforestation and concrete surfaces require understanding that these BLOCK infiltration. After completion, ask students what all helpful actions have in common (they help water seep into the ground).
instructions_for_student: Sort these 9 actions into two groups: actions that HARM groundwater (deplete it) and actions that HELP groundwater (recharge it). For each action, think: does this INCREASE or DECREASE the amount of water seeping into the ground? Tap a card, then tap the correct category bin to sort it — or drag and drop!
iconApproach: All icons are inline SVG components (IconCheck, IconX, IconRotateCcw, IconChevronLeft, IconChevronRight, IconDroplets, IconBookOpen, IconTarget, IconZap, IconFlaskConical). No external icon library (e.g. lucide-react) is required — the component is fully self-contained.

learn.description: Step-by-step explanation of groundwater, depletion causes, and rainwater harvesting. Each step has an animated cross-section illustration. Step 2 features a fully animated bore-well pump SVG scene with motor vibration, handle rocking, piston movement, water stream from spout, underground pipe flow, rising bubbles, and a sinking water table.

completionSummary.keyInsight: All helpful actions share one thing in common: they help water seep into the ground (infiltration).

defaultActions.label: Excessive Bore Wells
defaultActions.explanation: Too many bore wells pump out groundwater faster than it can naturally recharge, lowering the water table.
defaultActions.hint: Think: Are we taking water OUT of the ground or putting it IN?

defaultActions.label: Deforestation
defaultActions.explanation: Without tree roots, rainwater runs off the surface instead of seeping deep into the ground.
defaultActions.hint: Think: Do tree roots help or block water from going underground?

defaultActions.label: Concrete Surfaces
defaultActions.explanation: Concrete and asphalt are impermeable — they block rainwater from infiltrating into the soil below.
defaultActions.hint: Think: Does concrete let water pass through or block it?

defaultActions.label: Industrial Overuse
defaultActions.explanation: Factories and industries often pump massive amounts of groundwater, depleting it rapidly.
defaultActions.hint: Think: Do industries put water back into the ground or take it out?

defaultActions.label: Rainwater Harvesting
defaultActions.explanation: Collecting and directing rainwater into the ground helps replenish underground aquifers.
defaultActions.hint: Think: Where does the collected rainwater go — drains or underground?

defaultActions.label: Recharge Pits
defaultActions.explanation: Recharge pits are dug specifically to allow surface water to percolate down and replenish groundwater.
defaultActions.hint: Think: What is the purpose of digging these special pits?

defaultActions.label: Planting Trees
defaultActions.explanation: Tree roots create channels in the soil that help water seep through into underground aquifers.
defaultActions.hint: Think: What do tree roots do to the soil structure?

defaultActions.label: Open Soil / Permeable Surfaces
defaultActions.explanation: Open soil and permeable surfaces allow rainwater to naturally infiltrate and recharge groundwater.
defaultActions.hint: Think: Can water pass through open soil easily?

defaultActions.label: Check Dams
defaultActions.explanation: Check dams slow down flowing water, giving it time to seep into the ground and recharge aquifers.
defaultActions.hint: Think: What happens when flowing water is slowed down near soil?

visualLayout.groundPlacement: All trees, houses, and objects are positioned using CSS calc() relative to the ground surface line. For example top: calc(30% - 34px) anchors a 32px-tall tree so its base sits exactly on the 30% ground line. The ground surface is marked by a solid green gradient strip with grass emoji patches.

pumpScene.svgCoverage: Full scene height, 70% width, centered horizontally
pumpScene.pumpBaseY: y=86 in SVG (aligns with 32% ground line)
pumpScene.pipeExtent: y=96 to y=257 (from base through soil and rock into aquifer)
pumpScene.surfaceElements: House at calc(32% - 30px), tree at calc(32% - 34px), smaller tree at calc(32% - 24px), grass patches at calc(32% - 4px)

defaultCrossSection.surfaceElements: Tree1 at calc(30% - 34px), tree2 at calc(30% - 26px), tree3 at calc(30% - 32px), house at calc(30% - 24px), grass patches at calc(30% - 4px)

summaryCrossSections.depletedSide: Sky (#fef2f2) 0-30%, soil/rock below. Ground line at 30% with stump, factory, construction on surface. Water table at 20% (red).
summaryCrossSections.rechargedSide: Sky (#f0fdf4) 0-30%, soil/rock below. Ground line at 30% with trees and house on surface, rain drops. Water table at 65% (green).

interactionMethods.dragAndDrop: Mouse/touch drag from center cards to left/right bins. Ghost card follows cursor at fixed position with rotation and elevation. Bins scale up and change opacity on hover.
interactionMethods.tapToSort: Tap a card to select it (highlighted with primary color border and shadow). Then tap a bin to place it. Selection toggles on second tap.

feedbackSystem.correct: Card removed from center, inserted into bin with dropIn animation. Green banner shows check icon + Correct + explanation text. Banner auto-dismisses after 3s.
feedbackSystem.incorrect: Card shakes in place (shakeX, 0.5s). Red banner shows X icon + Not quite + hint text. Banner auto-dismisses after 3s.
feedbackSystem.completion: Score reaches 9/9 then 0.8s delay then completed flag then triggerCelebration (40 confetti particles, 4s) then 1.5s delay then showSummary flag then split-screen summary with key insight.
